title: Crypto Up/DOWN markets Binance Low Latency Feed
author: kabiraftab198
selftext:
I've been experimenting quite a bit with these markets, backtesting different strategies and even reverse-engineering some profitable traders.

The frustrating part? A lot of these strategies look great in backtests, but once you take them live, latency eats up most of the edge.

So I decided to take things a step further. Got KYC-approved and moved into colocation. It definitely helped, but the same problem remained. By the time my signals triggered, the fastest traders had already acted on that information. And by the time my orders actually got matched, either the price had already moved or most of the potential profit was gone.

That eventually led me down the rabbit hole of premium fiber routes between Binance (Tokyo) and London, trying to get the market data as fast as possible. So far what I have gathered it reduces London-Tokyo one-way trip from 105ms to 70ms giving us edge for 30-35ms.

The problem is that these dedicated low-latency routes are ridiculously expensive for an individual trader. And considering how many people could potentially benefit from the same feed, paying for the entire thing alone doesn't make much sense.

I'm planning to get one of these connections next week anyway, but figured I'd see if there are a few other serious traders interested in sharing the cost.

If you're working on latency-sensitive strategies and think faster Binance market data in London could help, feel free to DM me. We can discuss the setup, expected latency, and whether splitting the expenses makes sense.

Not selling a strategy or promising anyone an edge here. Just looking to share infrastructure costs with people who might actually find it useful.
